tasks.short: Find logistics cost and process opportunities.

steps.what: Pull lane cost and volume into one table.
Rank lanes whose unit cost beats the agreed rate.
Judge which process improvement opportunities are real.
Check the opportunity note before it is sent.
Send the opportunity note once the analyst has checked it.

tasks.design: A scheduled extract on {ERP} builds the lane cost table in {BI}. The analyst keeps only the opportunities the floor can actually change. {EMAIL} sends the note after that check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lane costs lived in a private spreadsheet, so a high unit cost and a real constraint looked the same.
tasks.enabler_now: Shipment cost and the contracted rate now sit in fields a view can rank.
tasks.still_hard: A cheap lane can still be the wrong lane when the dock or the customer window cannot move.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst has stood on that dock and knows which saving the site will refuse.

ambition.what: Revisit the worst lanes every month instead of once a year.

tasks.altitude: The week still includes saying no to a saving that breaks the floor. The ranking itself is no longer typed.

reach.task: Reprice a lane the analyst has kept
reach.learn: Which cost fields must be present before a lane is ranked

evidence.claim: Comparing a lane cost with a contracted rate is a table check. A floor walk is not.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from shipment cost to a checked opportunity note. Changing the contract is a different task.
Test the existing {ERP} and {BI} views before any custom extract.
Structured fields are lane id, unit cost, volume and contracted rate. The shipment extract produces them. Fallback: a lane with no rate is listed as missing, not as a saving.
EU data-protection rules apply. A study of named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Which lanes the customer will allow the analyst to reopen.
research_questions: How often a ranked lane is rejected because the rate file is stale.

already_counted.description: Judging which ranked lanes are real opportunities

incremental.description: Keep the contracted-rate map aligned with the current agreements

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A complete rate file saves the ranking and the send. The judgement stays. The low case is a month of lanes with no contracted rate.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Interpret logistics data across the chain.

steps.what: Pull forecasting and inventory figures for the lanes.
Sum transportation cost against the forecast volume.
Flag procurement lines that miss the inventory plan.
Interpret warehousing and manufacturing exceptions.
Check the logistics interpretation before it is filed.
File the interpretation on the planning record.

tasks.design: Forecast, inventory and purchase lines are read from {ERP} into {BI}. The analyst interprets the exceptions. The note is filed only after that check.
tasks.previous_blocker: Each function kept its own extract, so transportation and warehousing were explained in different meetings.
tasks.enabler_now: Those extracts now share a lane id and a week.
tasks.still_hard: A number can be right and still misread the reason a warehouse missed the plan.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst can tell a forecast error from a dock that was already full.

ambition.what: Read the same lane across forecast, stock and freight each week.

tasks.altitude: Interpretation of the exception stays. Pulling the four extracts does not.

reach.task: Correct a forecast the interpretation has questioned
reach.learn: Which forecast fields the logistics note relies on

evidence.claim: Comparing a lane cost with a contracted rate is a table check. A floor walk is not.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from the weekly extracts to a filed interpretation. Changing the forecast is the planner's task.
Test the existing {ERP} and {BI} views before any custom extract.

Structured fields are lane id, week, forecast quantity, inventory quantity, purchase-line status and transport cost. Each source system produces its own field. Fallback: a missing week is shown as a gap.
EU data-protection rules apply. A study of named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether manufacturing exceptions are visible in the same week as the freight.
research_questions: How often the interpretation changes the planner's next forecast.

incremental.description: Keep the lane-id map across forecast, stock and freight

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week with complete extracts saves the sums and the filing. The interpretation stays. The low case is a week whose forecast and stock do not share a lane id.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Read production volumes and the facility constraints.
Walk the production facilities the design must fit.
Sketch lane flows from the volume table.
Choose conceptual designs for those production facilities.
Check the logistic strategies against the walk.
Issue the conceptual design to the project file.

tasks.design: Volumes come from {ERP}. The analyst walks the facilities and chooses the conceptual design. {PROJECT} receives the design only after the walk is in the note.
tasks.previous_blocker: Designs were drawn from last year's volume sheet without a current walk.
tasks.enabler_now: The volume file and a short constraint list can be prepared before the walk.
tasks.still_hard: A drawing that ignores a column, a door or a neighbour is not a design.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst sees the constraint the volume file does not name.
tasks.altitude: The walk and the choice of design stay. The flow sketch from the volume table does not.

reach.task: Turn the conceptual design into a buildable layout
reach.learn: Which constraints the walk recorded and which it did not

evidence.claim: Comparing a lane cost with a contracted rate is a table check. A floor walk is not.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from volumes and a walk to an issued conceptual design. Detailed engineering is out of scope.
Test the existing {ERP} and {BI} views before any custom extract.

Structured fields are facility id, weekly volume, constraint type and source. The volume file produces the quantities. Fallback: a constraint seen only on the walk is typed by the analyst and marked unverified.
EU data-protection rules apply. A study of named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether the facilities may be walked before the design is requested.
research_questions: How often a walk overturns the flow sketch.

already_counted.description: Choosing the design after the facility walk

incremental.description: Keep the constraint types aligned with the sites in scope

approvals.approved_version: strategy note checked against the walk

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Known volumes save the sketch and the filing. The walk and the design choice stay. The low case is a facility the analyst has not walked.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Run logistics studies from floor times.

steps.what: Time the floor flow for the logistics studies.
Compute rate and network cost from the floor times.
Judge which analyses hold once the floor times are in.
Write the study note from the kept analyses.

tasks.design: The analyst times the flow in person. {SPREADSHEET} computes the rate and the network cost from those times. The study note keeps only the analyses the times support.
tasks.previous_blocker: Studies were rebuilt in a spreadsheet from memory of the floor.
tasks.enabler_now: A rate card and a timed sample can be calculated without retyping.
tasks.still_hard: A time study of named people is monitoring, and a short sample can misread a shift.
tasks.human_edge: The analyst knows when the timed hour was not a normal hour.
tasks.altitude: Timing the floor and judging the analyses stay. The arithmetic does not.

reach.task: Explain a slow step the study timed
reach.learn: Which shifts were timed and which were not

evidence.claim: Comparing a lane cost with a contracted rate is a table check. A floor walk is not.

assumptions: Focal role is the logistics analyst. Boundary: from a timed sample to a study note. Redesigning the floor is a different task.
Test the existing {ERP} and {BI} views before any custom extract.
Structured fields are step id, observed minutes, sample size and rate. The analyst enters the times. Fallback: a step not timed is omitted, not given an average.
EU data-protection rules apply. A study of named people needs works-council consent where national rules require it.
unknowns: Whether timing named people is allowed on this site, and for which shifts.
research_questions: How large a sample the supervisor will accept before a change.

already_counted.description: Judging which analyses the floor times support

incremental.description: Keep the rate card matched to the steps being timed

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A clean rate card saves the arithmetic. The timing and the judgement stay. The low case is a shift that was not a normal hour. No other role's time is in this task.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Floor walks, interviews and the choice of which saving is real stay with the analyst. Standard lane costs and indicator refreshes leave the spreadsheet.
reach: Warehouse supervisors, on which floor facts a flow study needs.
Transport planners, on which rate fields a lane comparison needs.
skills_to_grow: Marking a missing rate instead of filling it.
Separating a floor constraint from a model result.
role.ambitious_version: A lane exception arrives with its cost, its floor note and the name of the person who may change the plan.
